This is petition filed under Section 22 of The Employee's Compensation Act, 1923, seeking compensation of Rs.13,38,675/- from the respondents, on account of death of Rudresh, who is husband of petitioner No.1 and father of petitioners No.2 and 3, arisen out of and in the course of employment under respondents No.1 and 2.
2.

The brief facts of the case are as follows:
The deceased Rudresh was working with the respondent No.1 and 2 as a driver-cum-loader.

On 29-08- 2020, the respondent No.1 and 2 have engaged the deceased Rudresh as a goods loader in one of their goods vehicle bearing No.KA-11-B-1267 and as per their directions he proceeded to distribute the goods to respondent No.3, who is one of customer/client of respondents No.1 and 2.
While the deceased Rudresh was unloading the heavy packed goods in the aforesaid company, the said goods fell on his leg.

Due to which his leg was injured and he was shifted to local hospital for Rudresh Since Dead, Represented By Its ... vs Swaha Dazzle Designs on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165503793/
2 treatment. Thereafter he was shifted to Kusuma Hospital, Bengaluru, for further treatment.

sentences.text: The doctor who treated the deceased has given a report stating that, the right leg of the deceased has suffered gangrene due to injuries sustained in the said accident.

As per the medical report of the Bhavasara Clinic, the petitioners have approached the respondent No.1 and 2 and informed about the health condition of Rudresh and requested for financial help and other guidance.

At that stage the respondent No.1 and 2 suggested the petitioners to admit the deceased Rudresh in Rangadorai Hospital, Chamarajpet, for further treatment and assured the petitioners that they will take care of his medical expenses.

As per their suggestion, the petitioners admitted him at Rangadorai Hospital,
but the respondents No.1 and 2 did not pay any medical bills, nor they came to see the deceased.
Further they did nor care to receive the calls of the petitioners.
Due to injuries suffered the deceased Rudresh died on 17-10-2020.

The accident has occurred during the course of employment at the place of respondents client/customer i.e. respondent No.3 and the accident has occurred due to the negligence of the respondent No.1 and 2, as they have not taken any safety measures for their employee, as per settled position of law.
The petitioners have approached the respondent No.1 and 2 for compensation, since the death has occurred during the course of employment.
But, they have neither settled any monetary benefits, not they paid the medical bills to the petitioners.
Earlier to the accident the deceased was working as driver- cum-loader with the respondent No.1 and 2 and was getting a salary of Rs.18,000/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Jigani Police have registered the NCR No.682/2020 dated 03-12-2020.

As per the notification No.
S.O.71E of 2020, notififed under Section 4(1B) of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923, an amount of Rs.15,000/- is to be considered as wages for the purpose of computation of compensation.

As the age of deceased Rudresh at the time of accident was 42 years and the relevant factor for computation being 178.49, as per Schedule IV of the Employeed Compensation Act, 1923,
the respondent No.1 and 2 are the employer of the deceased and the respondent No.3 is the customer/client of respondent No.1 and 2, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.13,38,675/- to the petitioners.

Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.13,38,675/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3.
On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 to 3 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 and 2 in their written statement have denied all the allegations made in the petition.
They have contended that, the petition is barred by limitation and therefore suffers from delay and latches.
The police NCR was registered on 03-10-2020, but the present petition is filed on 30-09-20203, after a lapse of 1128 days i.e. more than 3 years.
The alleged accident has occurred on 29-08-2020 and the said Rudresh has allegedly died on 17-10-2020.

Further it is contended that,
the goods vehicle in which the said Rudresh was allegedly engaged to work as goods loader does not belong to the respondent No.1 and 2.
The said vehicle belongs to one Chandra B.P. and not the respondents.
Hence, the question of engaging the Rudresh never arose.

Further it is contended that,
the alleged accident took place on 29-08- 2020, however no accident was reported.
The death allegedly has occurred on 17-10-2020, but the complaint is lodged on 03-12-2020, after a lapse of more than 2 months.
They have denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased.

Further it is contended that, even otherwise the boxes are not heavy, the boxes contain steel diya's of size 180 Rudresh Since Dead, Represented By Its ... vs Swaha Dazzle Designs on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165503793/
3 grams, they were packed into boxes of 10 pairs of diya's each.
Thus, the weight of each box was approximately 2 kilograms, inclusive of carton weight and the size of box was 9 inches x 8 inches x 5.5 inches and the box was made of paper carton.
As such the said box is not capable of causing such a grave injury so as to lead to death or disablement of any kind.
On the said date the respondent No.1 and 2 had entrusted the transportation to M/s Porter, a transportation company and the unloading charges were paid to one Chandrappa.
They did not engage anyone else for unloading.
Further it is contended that, the respondent No.2 owns a Maruthi van with Reg. No.KA-05-MY- 3347 for her personal use.
The said Rudresh had been appointed to drive the said personal vehicle only and he was never engaged as loader or driver-cum-loader or to transport goods by the respondent No.1.
When the alleged accident occurred, the said Rudresh was not in the employment of the respondents.
He may have suffered injury while working for some other employer or on his own self employment.
Further it is contended that, after accident the deceased had not filed any complaint during his lifetime.
Long after the death of the said Rudresh, the petitioners have filed the present frivolous complaint with the sole object of extorting money from them.
After registering the NCR, the police have not filed any FIR, since no substance was found in the complaint.

Further it is contended that, according to the medical records produced by the petitioners, the Rudresh went to Kusuma Hospital on 29-08-2020 with complaint of wound over right foot/blackish discoloration of right 2nd and 3 toes and nothing more.
Obviously the only injury that alleged to have caused to Rudresh was minor injury to the 2nd and 3rd toes of the right foot, which do not cause disability or death.

From the medical records produced by the petitioners it is also obvious that the said Rudresh was suffering from diabetes before accident and the petitioners may have neglected to provide treatment to him.
The respondents cannot be held responsible for the petitioners own mistake.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Whereas, the respondent No.3 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has contended that, it is one of the customers of the respondent No.1 and 2.

Pursuant to the purchase order placed to respondent No.1, the goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-11- EB-1267 had come to the premises of respondent No.3 in order to supply the products as per purchase order dated 29- 08-2020.
It has denied that, the deceased Rudresh had come in the said goods vehicle and distributed the products to it.
Further it is contended that, no accident has occurred within the premises of respondent No.3 on 29-08-2020.
The deceased Rudresh was never an employee of respondent No.3.
Admittedly he is alleged to be an employee of respondents No.1 and 2.
Hence, the respondent No.3 is not liable to pay any compensation under the provisions of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923.
Further it is contended that, the claim of the petitioners is not maintainable, as the same is barred by limitation and the reasons assigned in the affidavit,
accompanying the application filed under Section 5 of Limitation Act, does not amount to a sufficient cause to seek condonation of delay in filing the present petition.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES Rudresh Since Dead, Represented By Its ... vs Swaha Dazzle Designs on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165503793/
4
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, there was employee and employer relationship between the deceased Rudresh and the respondent Nos.1 and 2?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that, during the course of employment Rudresh succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that occurred on 29-08-2020 ?

3. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
4. What order or Award ?
ADDITIONAL ISSUE 1.
Whether the petition is barred by limitation ?
7. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 has got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined herself as R.W.1 and got marked 5 documents as Ex.R.1 to 5.
The respondent No.3 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.
8. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

In support of his arguments, the learned counsel for petitioners has relied on the following decisions:

9. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Rudresh Since Dead, Represented By Its ... vs Swaha Dazzle Designs on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165503793/
5
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Affirmative Issue No.3: Partly Affirmative Additional Issue: Negative.

Issue No.4: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 & 2: As both these issues are connected to each other, in order to avoid repetition of facts and circumstances of the case and for better appreciation of evidence on record, I take both the issues together for common discussion.
11. It is specific case of the petitioners that, the deceased Rudresh was working with the respondent No.1 and 2 as a driver-cum-loader.
On 29-08-2020, the respondent No.1 and 2 have engaged the deceased Rudresh to load goods in one of their goods vehicle bearing No.KA-11-B-1267.
As per the directions of respondent No.1 & 2, he proceeded to distribute the goods to respondent No.3, who is one of the customer/client of respondent No.1 and 2.
While the deceased Rudresh was unloading the heavy packed goods in the aforesaid company, the said goods fell on his right leg and he sustained injury.
Due to which he has suffered gangrene on the injured part of right leg and died on 17-10- 2020.

Further it is contended that, though initially the respondent No.1 and 2 have assured the petitioners that they will pay the medical expenses of the deceased Rudesh, they did not turn back to pay the medical bills and even they did not come to see the deceased.

The accident has occurred during the course of employment at the place of respondents client/customer i.e. respondent No.3 and the said accident has occurred due to the negligence of the respondents No.1 and 2, as they have not taken any safety measures for their employee.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident the deceased was working as driver-cum-loader with the respondents No.1 and 2 and was getting a salary of Rs.18,000/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.

The respondents No.1 and 2 being the employer of the deceased and the respondent No.3 being the customer/client of respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

12. In order to claim compensation under Sec.22 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, the foremost burden on the petitioners is to establish that, as on the alleged date, time and place of accident, the deceased was an employee of the respondent No.1 and 2 and as per their instructions he was engaged in the work of unloading the goods from vehicle bearing No.KA-11-B-1267.

In other words, the petitioners are required to prove that, at the time of accident there was an employer and employee relationship between the deceased Rudresh and the respondents No.1 and 2.
13.

In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 has got examined herself as P.W.1 by filing her examination-in- chief affidavit, wherein she has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of their oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked total 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to 14.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 to 3 are notarized copy of Aadhar cards of petitioners, Ex.P.4 are prescriptions (total 5), Ex.P.5 are medical bills (total 7), Ex.P.6 is medical certificate of cause of death, Ex.P.7 is death certificate, Ex.P.8 is compliance letter under RTI Act,
Rudresh Since Dead, Represented By Its ... vs Swaha Dazzle Designs on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165503793/
6 Ex.P.9 is true copy of police acknowledgment, Ex.P.10 is true copy of complaint, Ex.P.11 is notice dated 24-07-2023, Ex.P.12 are postal receipts, Ex.P.13 are postal acknowledgement cards and Ex.P.14 is reply notice dated 22-08-2023.

14. On meticulously going through the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners, prima-facia it reveals that, as on the alleged date, time and place of accident, the deceased was an employee of the respondents No.1 and 2 and as per their instructions he was engaged in the work of unloading the goods from vehicle bearing No.KA-11-B-1267.

Further it reveals that, while the deceased Rudresh was unloading the goods in the respondent No.3 company,
the carton boxes containing goods fell on his right leg and he sustained injury.
Later he suffered gangrene on the injured portion of the right leg and died on 17-10-2020.

15. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the instant case, there is no dispute that, as on the date of accident the deceased Rudresh was the employee of respondent No.1 &
2.

Further, it is also not disputed that, on the alleged date, time and place of accident, the respondent No.1 & 2 have delivered goods to the respondent No.3 company in the goods vehicle bearing No.KA-11-B-1267.

But, the respondent No.1 & 2 specifically deny that, at the time of alleged accident they had engaged the deceased Rudresh for the work of driver-cum-loader of goods vehicle bearing No.KA- 11-B-1267, to transport the goods to their customer/respondent No.3.
Further they have contended that, the deceased Rudresh was appointed only to drive the Maruti Van bearing No.KA-05-MY-3347 owned by the respondent No.2 for her personal use and no other vehicle.

Further it is contended that, on the alleged date of accident they had entrusted the transportation of goods to respondent No.3 to one of the transportation company M/s Porter and the unloading charges were paid to one Chandrappa.
At the time of alleged accident the said Rudresh was not under their employment and he might have suffered injury while working for some other employer or while on his own self employment.
Further it is contended that, the boxes contain steel Diya's of size 180 grams, packed into boxes of 10 pairs of Diya's each, each box weighs approximately 2 kilograms inclusive of carton weight.
As such, the said box is not capable of causing such a grave injury, so as to lead to death or disablement of any kind.

16. As per Section 106 of The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, the burden of proof as to any particular fact lies on that person who wishes the Court to believe in its existence, unless it is provided by any law that the proof of that fact shall lie on any particular person.
Therefore, the burden of proving the above alleged specific contentions/defence taken by the respondent No.1 & 2 in the instant case, was on the respondent No.1 & 2.
But, the respondent No.1 & 2 have failed to discharge the said burden.

Except the self serving statements of the R.W.1/respondent No.2, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the respondent No.1 & 2 have appointed the deceased Rudresh only to drive the Maruti Van bearing No.KA-05-MY-3347 owned by the respondent No.2 for her personal use and not for any other vehicle and on the alleged date of accident they had entrusted the transportation of goods to one of the transportation company M/s Porter and the unloading charges were paid to one Chandrappa.

The respondent No.1 & 2 have produced two payment vouchers, which are marked as Ex.R.4, to establish the alleged fact that, on the alleged date of accident they had engaged one Rudresh Since Dead, Represented By Its ... vs Swaha Dazzle Designs on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165503793/
7 Chandru to deliver the goods to respondent No.3.

sentences.text: But, it is pertinent to note that, the said vouchers neither contains the name of the firm or organisation which has issued the same, nor it contains the seal, registration number or establishment number of that particular firm or organisation.

Even,
they have not made any efforts to prove the contents of said documents by examining the author of said documents.
In such circumstances, the said documents have no value in the eye of law.
It is settled proposition of law that, mere production and marking of documents in the evidence do not constitute proof of their contents.

Further, there is absolutely no evidence placed on record by the respondents to establish that, at the time of alleged accident the said Rudresh was not under their employment and he has suffered injury while working for some other employer or while on his own self employment.

Further, there is no evidence placed on record to show that, the carton boxes alleged to contain steel Diya's of size 180 grams were weighing just 2 kilograms inclusive of carton weight and as such the said boxes even if fell on the leg of a person they do not cause such a grave injury, so as to lead to death or disablement of any kind.

17. On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners and the admissions given by the respondent No.2/R.W.1 in her cross- examination, clearly establishes that, as on the alleged date, time and place of accident the deceased Rudresh was an employee of the respondents No.1 and 2, working as driver- cum-loader of goods and as per instructions of respondent No.1 & 2 he was engaged in the work of transportation of goods to their customer/client respondent No.3, in the vehicle bearing No.KA-11-B-1267.
While unloading the goods from the said vehicle in the respondent No.3 company premises, the carton boxes containing goods fell on his right leg and he sustained injury.
Due to said injury, he suffered gangrene on the injured portion of the right leg and died on 17-10-2020.

The Ex.P.6 medical certificate of cause of death, issued by the Kusuma Hospital, Bengaluru, clearly speaks that, due to severe Diabetes Mellitus, Gangrene of Right Leg and Sepsis the injured Rudresh has died.
This clearly goes to show that, the deceased Rudresh has died due to injuries suffered in the accident in question and not due to any other injury or cause.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, it is not the case of respondents that, the deceased has sustained injuries in some other accident, other than the accident in question or he has died due to some other cause, other than the cause mentioned in Ex.P.6 Medical Certificate.
18.
No doubt, the accident has taken place on 29-08-2020 and deceased Rudresh has died on 17-10-2020 i.e. after lapse of 01 month 19 days from the date of accident.
But, there is clear nexus between the injury caused to the deceased Rudresh and cause of his death.

The medical records of the deceased clearly speaks that, due to injury sustained to the right leg of the Rudresh in the accident taken place on 29-08-2020, he has suffered gangrene and it has resulted in his death on 17-10-2020.
There is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the contents of said document.

Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the deceased Rudresh has died due to injuries sustained in the accident taken place on 29-08- 2020 in the premises of respondent No.3 company, while the deceased was engaged in the work of transportation and unloading of goods in the vehicle bearing No.KA-11-B- 1267, as per the instructions of his employer respondent No.1 & 2.
19.
It is settled proposition of law that, strict proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required in the claim petition under Employees' Compensation Act.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in various decisions Rudresh Since Dead, Represented By Its ... vs Swaha Dazzle Designs on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165503793/
8 has consistently held that, the standard of preponderance of probability suffices to establish facts such as employer-employee relationship and injury caused during the course of employment.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This approach balances fairness and practicality, recognizing that civil compensation proceedings do not demand the same rigorous proof as in criminal trials.

Therefore, the claimants need only to demonstrate that, their version of events is more probable than not, facilitating access to compensation without the burden of strict standards of proof as in criminal trials.

20. Therefore, in the light of settled propositions of law and for the reasons stated above, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that, as on the date of accident there was employee and employer relationship between the deceased Rudresh and the respondent No.1 and 2 and he has died due to injuries sustained in the accident, arisen out of and in the course of employment under respondent No.1 & 2, on 29-08-2020.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 and 2 in Affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:

While answering above issues this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioners have successfully proved that, there was an employee and employer relationship between the deceased Rudresh and the respondent No.1 & 2 and he has died due to injuries sustained during the course of employment under the respondent No.1 & 2, when he was engaged in unloading goods from the vehicle bearing No. KA-11B-1267.

Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation for the death of Rudresh, arisen out of and in the course of employment under the respondent No.1 & 2.
Now the petitioners are required to establish that, they are the legal representatives of the deceased.
In this regard, they have produced their respective Aadhar cards, which are marked as Ex.P.1 to 3.
The said documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioner No.1 is wife and petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children of deceased Rudresh.

On the other hand, the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased Rudresh is not specifically denied by the respondents and even there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents with respect to same.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners and hold that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of deceased Nagaraju.

22. As per Sec.4 of Employees Compensation Act, the amount of compensation to be paid in case of death is an amount equal to fifty percent of the monthly wages of the deceased [employee]
multiplied by the relevant factor or an amount of one lakh and twenty thousand rupees, whichever is more.
Therefore, the burden was on the petitioners to establish the actual monthly income of the deceased, as on the date of accident.

The petitioners have contended that, before accident the deceased was working as driver-cum- loader with the respondent No.1 & 2 and was drawing salary of Rs.18,000/- per month and was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, before accident the deceased was working as driver-cum- loader with the respondent No.1 & 2.
But, the petitioners have failed to establish the income of the deceased.

Except the self serving statements of the petitioners, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners to show that, the respondent No.1 & 2 were paying salary of Rs.18,000/- per month to the deceased.

In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the minimum wages notified by the Central Government in the Official Gazette for that particular Rudresh Since Dead, Represented By Its ... vs Swaha Dazzle Designs on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165503793/
9 year.

As per the notification No. S.O.71E of 2020, notified under Section 4(1B) of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923, an amount of Rs.15,000/- is to be considered as wages for the purpose of computation of compensation.
Therefore, the income of the deceased Nagaraju as on the date of accident is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.
23. The petitioners have averred that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 42 years.
To substantiate the same, the petitioners have not produced any authenticate document.

But, as per Ex.P.6 Medical Certificate of Cause of Death, issued by the Kusuma Hospital, Bengaluru, as on the date of his death the deceased Rudresh was aged about 44 years and his date of birth is mentioned 23-05-1976.
There is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the said document and the oral evidence of P.W.1.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, the date of birth of deceased Rudresh mentioned in the Ex.P.6 is not specifically denied or disputed by the respondents.
Admittedly, the accident has taken place on 29-08-2020.

Therefore, in such circumstances, taking into consideration the date of birth of deceased Rudresh as mentioned in the Ex.P.6 Medical Certificate,
the age of the deceased as on the date of accident is considered as 44 years.

24. As per Sec.4 of Employees Compensation Act, the amount of compensation to be paid in case of death is an amount equal to fifty percent of the monthly wages of the deceased [employee]
multiplied by the relevant factor or an amount of one lakh and twenty thousand rupees, whichever is more.
As on the date of accident the age of the deceased was 49 years.
The relevant factor given to his age in the Fourth Schedule of the Act is 172.52.
The monthly salary of the deceased is held at Rs.15,000/-.
Fifty percent of the same will be Rs.7,500/-.
If the same is multiplied by the relevant factor 172.52, it comes to Rs.12,93,900/-.
Accordingly, it is held that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.12,93,900/-.

In addition to the said compensation, as per Section 4(4) of Employees Compensation Act, coupled with Official Gazette Notification No.45/2009 dated 18-01-2010, a sum of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards funeral expenditure.

Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.12,98,900/-, for the death of Rudresh, in the accident arisen out of and in the course of employment under respondent No.1 & 2.
25.
Liability:

The evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the accident has occurred during the course of employment under respondent No.1 & 2 and the deceased Rudresh has succumbed to the injuries sustained in the said accident arisen out of and in the course of employment under respondents No.1 and 2.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the employer of the deceased are vicariously liable to compensate the petitioners for the death of Rudresh.
